column5: Team member running this interview (leave blank if you are self-completing)
column6: W1. How do this year's total sales and cases sold compare with three years ago, and which moved more?
column7: W2. Over those same three years, what happened to your tasting-room visits and to what an average visitor spends?
column8: W3. How has your wine club changed over three years, in both the number of members and the share who renew each year?
column9: W4. Who buys your wine today, and how is that different from three years ago?
column10: W5. Have you had club members or regular buyers cancel or drift away recently? If so, what did they tell you when they left?
column11: W6. In the last two years, have you changed any prices, run discounts, or changed your tasting fee? For each change, what happened to volume or visits afterward?
column12: W7. What have you tried in the last three years to bring in sales or new customers? For each thing, roughly what did it cost, what happened, and are you still doing it?
column13: W8. For any lesser-known grapes or unusual bottlings you make, how do their sell-through and margin compare with your flagship, and who buys them?
column14: W9. What share of your revenue is direct versus wholesale, how has that share moved over three years, and what happened to total revenue as it shifted?
column15: W10. Which wineries do you notice doing best right now, whatever their size, and what do you see them doing differently?
column16: W11. Since the 2025 crush, have you changed where you get your fruit, bought any grapes on the spot market, or renegotiated contracts?
column17: W12. When customers talk to you about their wine buying, what do they say? Tell me about the last few conversations.
column18: Who else should we talk to? If you can, a name and an introduction helps a lot.
column19: What have you tried or innovated recently? Tell us in your own words about any new approaches, experiments, or ideas you've put into practice.
column21: Who is buying, and who left?

column19: We have strived to deliver a wine that is truly a great value. Putting the vineyards first and taking unique approaches to ensure each wine has its own identity. We use an Austrian oak barrel for our Sauvignon Blanc, similar to French oak but less expensive. We co-ferment red varietals like Charbono and Petite Sirah, harkening back to the old ways in Napa. Our Cabernet Sauvignon is picked with freshness and balance in mind.
